matched.title: Path payment strict-send reported with destination asset but source amount

findings.title: Path payment strict-send reported with destination asset but source amount
SEP-45 validate issues a JWT without requiring a server-signed authorization entry
Signed XDR threshold bytes are read as negative ints, so SEP-10 medium threshold can be bypassed on RPC-backed deployments
Shared API key compared with non-constant-time String.equals
Header-signed JWT accepted without audience, identifier or lifetime binding, so one signed token can be replayed as a session
SEP-45 challenge signs RPC-supplied server auth entries without checking invoked contract, function or sub-invocations
Empty client_domain is routed to the custodial branch but validated with a null key
SEP-31 strict-send accepts a fee that makes amount_out zero or negative
Horizon getTransaction returns FAILED transactions as successful ledger transactions
SEP-31 PATCH without a fields object throws NullPointerException instead of a 400
Muxed destination M-address encoded from XDR layout (id before key)
Soroban transfer recognition ignores the contract ID, so any contract's transfer() is reported as a payment
RPC parser throws NullPointerException or IndexOutOfBounds on empty or [] bodies instead of a controlled error
SEP-10 validation skips client_domain signature check on existing accounts, so a JWT can claim any client domain
SEP-24 withdraw and deposit accept another user's SEP-38 quote without a creator check
SEP-12 id-path GET/PUT forwards the caller's memo unbound to the token memo
SEP-12 DELETE skips the memo check when the token is a muxed account matching the target account
SEP-45 challenge accepts any client_domain without the allowlist check that SEP-10 applies
SEP-31 accepts any SEP-38 quote by id without checking that the authenticated client created it
SEP-12 PUT writes to the business server before the SEP-31 customer-id ownership claim is checked
ApiKeyFilter logs full query string on every request, before authentication
JWT filter logs raw query string, including token query parameters, before authentication
client_domain is fetched over HTTP(S) with SSRF checks skipped on non-public networks and only a resolve-time check on mainnet
MEMO_ID accepts negative and out-of-range uint64 values without a range check
SEP-24 deposit stores the requester-supplied asset_issuer instead of the resolved asset's issuer
SEP-45 validate throws unhandled exceptions on malformed auth entries instead of returning a 400
getTransaction returns the RPC's transaction without checking that its hash matches the requested hash
getTrustlineRpc dereferences a possibly null entries list, unlike getAccountRpc
SEP-24 deposit and withdraw skip sign and precision checks on amount when no min or max is configured
SEP-24 deposit request counter is looked up but never incremented
SEP-31 fee from the /rate callback is applied without checking its asset matches the transaction asset
SEP-31 POST with a fiat asset code and an issuer throws ClassCastException
getField does not catch IllegalArgumentException or NullPointerException from field.get, so the default fallback does not apply
Operation source account ignored; from attributed to transaction source
Instance amount validator has no magnitude bound, so exponent-form amounts pass when no max is configured
Invalid base64 hash memo throws IllegalArgumentException, not a validation error
Hash memo string rendering differs: memoAsString returns hex, xdrMemoToString returns base64
ErrorHelper wraps reflective failures in a generic RuntimeException, hiding the requested exception type
findTarget dereferences a null property type and instantiates arbitrary no-arg classes on unknown paths
Empty or dot-only path throws an uncaught NoSuchElementException from the tokenizer
get() catches only ReflectiveOperationException, so beanutils runtime exceptions escape its Optional contract
Rejection of an invalid token relies on a NullPointerException thrown from the finally block
SEP-31 POST claims customer ids before the request is fully validated, with no rollback, and the sender claim persists if the receiver check fails
AuthHelper.forApiKey(header, key) ignores the configured header name and always sends X-Api-Key
submitTransaction returns ERROR and TRY_AGAIN_LATER results as ordinary responses and does not poll the hash to a final state
A SUCCESS transaction whose operations fail to parse is reported as not found, so pollers wait out their timeout
Contract transfer args indexed without length or type checks; runtime exception escapes poll
Generic reflective setter writes any reachable bean property from a dotted path with no allowlist
SEP-24 findTransaction lets any muxed sub-account of a G-account read transactions stored under the plain G-account
Customer-id ownership is keyed to the wallet client name, so every user of that client shares ownership of the customer id

findings.title: Signed SEP-10 challenge can be redeemed for JWTs repeatedly within its timebounds
SEP-45 validate consumes the challenge nonce before client signatures are verified, letting anyone burn a victim's challenge

failing_checks.title: Submission outcome
failing_checks.reason: submitTransaction (Horizon line 156) returns only the async status and does not poll. The polling path, waitForTransactionAvailable, accepts the first non-null getTransaction result. Horizon.getTransaction never checks `successful`, so a FAILED on-chain transaction is returned as a completed result.

failing_checks.reason: On a failed on-chain submission, the Horizon path returns the transaction as completed. A caller that records a payment as settled therefore marks a record paid that was not. failing_checks.title: Controls outside the prompt
failing_checks.reason: The rule that the server signs only the auth entries of the approved SEP-45 web-auth call is not enforced in code. The server signs any RPC-supplied entry whose credentials match its account, without checking the invoked contract, function, arguments or sub-invocations.

failing_checks.title: Stated purpose versus behaviour
failing_checks.reason: The service's stated amount validation (sign, precision, limits) runs only when a min or max is configured. For assets without limits, the claimed validation does not happen, so the stated behaviour is not delivered.

failing_checks.title: Core function works
failing_checks.reason: The core ledger read path does not work correctly as shipped. getTransaction returns FAILED Horizon transactions as successful ledger transactions, so the service can report a payment as settled when it failed on chain.
